minutes.headline: Committee backed a warrant article moving primary school climate-control money; Turkey Hill facilities plan debated.
minutes.summary: After an executive session on non-union negotiations, the committee heard the superintendent's report on busing, the facilities director search and heat. It reviewed the budget timeline and draft capital plan, with debate over Turkey Hill ADA work and later-year costs. It approved language for a special town meeting warrant article for the primary school, discussed goals and the improvement strategy, and agreed to form a Turkey Hill subcommittee.

what_happened.line: The School Committee voted to approve warrant article language for a special town meeting on primary school ductless split climate control, with a date correction.
The article asks town meeting to transfer money already in the FY23 capital plan to the school district; it was described as not new money.
Members discussed the draft capital plan, including Turkey Hill ADA work and a later-year renovation line that assumes state reimbursement; no action was taken.
The committee presented an FY25 budget timeline with requests due Nov 20, a first presentation Jan 17 and a final presentation and hearing March 20.
The committee agreed to form a Turkey Hill subcommittee and to take up Turkey Hill as a future agenda topic.

why_it_matters: The climate control article is a vote residents will be asked to take at special town meeting, and it moves existing capital money rather than adding to the tax bill, as described.
Turkey Hill's long-term cost is still unsettled, and the committee said it should be set out for the public, so a larger capital request may come later.
watch_next: The special town meeting vote on the primary school ductless split article.
The FY25 budget dates: requests due Nov 20, first presentation Jan 17, final presentation and hearing March 20.
